properties.description:
crates/reflow2-core/tests/sweep_coverage.rs, 6 cases.

WHAT IT PINS: that a level with components and no coupling between them is named as SILENT rather than clean; that a level which IS coupled is not named; that a rule which walked nothing is named while a rule with a population is not; that a reported population is the same number the rule actually walks, verified by adding a real edge and watching it move; and that every rule in `swept.rules` has a reported population, so no rule can go silently uncounted.

THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST is a_level_with_components_but_no_coupling_is_named_as_silent_not_clean. It reproduces the measured failure in miniature: components that ARE coupled, so the topology rules have a real population and report cleanly, sitting under subsystems that have no coupling at all. Before this, that graph produced a clean result a reader would take as covering the subsystems.

AND ONE THAT GUARDS THE SIGNAL RATHER THAN THE FINDING: a_level_holding_one_component_is_never_called_blind. A level with a single component cannot have a pair joining two components at it — arithmetic, not a modelling gap. Naming it would be the false positive that teaches a reader to skip the line, and a signal that cries wolf once is a signal nobody reads again. Found by running the check against a real graph rather than by reasoning about it.

NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be found: nothing verifies that the levels a project declares are the RIGHT levels, or that a coupled level is coupled CORRECTLY. This says what the sweep could not have spoken about; it does not judge the decomposition. And the populations are per-rule, not per-finding — a rule that walked a large population can still have skipped a corner of it that no level boundary describes.
properties.findings:
RUN 2026-08-20: 6 passed, 0 failed. Whole crate 1127 passed / 0 failed across 108 binaries — exactly +6 tests and +1 binary against the 1121/107 baseline.

EXERCISED ON THE LIVE GRAPH, not only fixtures. detect_defects over reflow2's own design now reports: duplicate 0 DUPLICATES edges (nothing to examine); circular_dependency 182 dependency pairs; and subsystem 10 components with 0 pairs between them. The coverage note reads 'the subsystem level has 10 component(s) and ZERO dependency pairs between them, so every topology result here — cycles, severability, single points of failure — is silent about that level rather than clean about it.' Both halves fire on real data, which is what says they are not theoretical.

THE NUMBER THAT PROVES THE SECOND MECHANISM WAS NEEDED: 182. The cycle rule walked a large, healthy population and reported cleanly. The approved first design — naming rules that had nothing to examine — would have printed NOTHING about it.

CAUGHT BY CLIPPY, RUN LOCALLY RATHER THAN BY CI: a collapsible if in the level-coupling loop failed -D warnings. That is the gate this project's own notes flag as the one forgotten twice; two minutes locally against a 20-minute cold-cache CI round trip.
properties.name: A sweep names the rules and levels it could not have spoken about
